newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: French, German interest in Argentine airports sale.
newsitem.headline: French, German interest in Argentine airports sale.

text.p: European investors have shown interest in the privatization of Argentina's 57 airports, Saul Bouer, the official in charge of the sale, said Friday.

"There are various groups interested, at least two French ones and one German," Bouer told the state-run Telam news agency from Paris, where he is accompanying Trade and Industry Secretary Alieto Guadagni.
Guadagni is on a visit to Europe to promote investment in Argentina's mining sector and airports.

Bouer suggested that one of the most serious contenders will be the company that runs Paris' airports. The operators of Frankfurt airport could also be a serious competitor in the tender, that is expected some time next year, according to Telam.
Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) is advising the Argentine government on the sale of the airports.
The investment necessary to bring the airports up to scratch has been estimated at $1.65 billion. The concessions will last for 25 years.
